nodes.title: START HERE
widgets_values:
# VIDEO – MiniMax H3
Prompt + references in, a shot with picture and sound out.

1. **Models** (group 1): download links are in the notes on the left.
2. **Settings** (group 3): **NAME** = output folder · **RESOLUTION**: aspect ratio + scale (1.0x = 1344×768, H3's trained size, for the film; fast test: scale *Custom*, custom_scale 0.67 = 896×512) · **Length** in seconds · **Seed** · **TURBO?** on = 8 fast steps, off = the official 50 steps (~3× slower).
3. **Prompt** (4a): **STYLE** and **WORLD** once, the shot in the green **THIS SHOT** box. Start from the *Presets* note.
4. **REF IMAGE 1–4** (4b): characters, places, storyboards. **START FRAME / END FRAME** (4f): the shot starts / ends exactly on this image (magenta notes drawn on a start frame vanish, the action follows them). Bypass every image you don't need (**Ctrl+B**).
5. **SWITCHES** (group 3): switch on what you use (below) and load its file.
6. Run. Check **LENGTH CHECK** (group 3) and **FINAL PROMPT** (group 5).

**Switches**
* **VOICE LINE?** (4e): your recording, pinned at frame 0: exact timing, the lips follow it.
* **AUDIO REFERENCE?** (4c): a voice; the character says *new* sentences in it.
* **VIDEO REFERENCE?** (4d): your acting or a Blender layout, used as set in **VIDEO REFERENCE MODE**: *Follow acting* (with the clip's sound) · *Exact layout* (frame-exact camera) · *Both*.
* **UPSCALE?** (7): the same shot at 2688×1536, with the same prompt and references.

**Output:** `output/AnimeH3/Video/NAME/` as MP4 (H.264, CRF 15, with sound): `NAME_00001.mp4`, `NAME_workflow_00001.png` (drag it in to get every setting back), `NAME_up_00001.mp4`.

**Watch out**
* H3 renders in 17-frame steps: Length snaps up to the next one (see LENGTH CHECK). With a voice line: Length = the line + the reaction.
* `<Picture N>` counts the active images in this order: START FRAME, then REF IMAGE 1–4. Bypassing one renumbers the rest.
* An audio reference must say a *different* sentence than the new line.

**Needs** ComfyUI 0.37.0 or newer + [KJNodes](https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes), [Mickmumpitz Nodes](https://github.com/mickmumpitz/ComfyUI-Mickmumpitz-Nodes), [rgthree](https://github.com/rgthree/rgthree-comfy), [MMH3 Ultimate Upscale](https://github.com/bbaudio-2025/Comfyui-MMH3-UltimateUpscale). Red nodes: *Missing Node Packs* → **Install All** → restart.

nodes.title: LENGTH CHECK (fills in after a run)
STYLE
widgets_values: 2D anime screencap, flat cel-shaded illustration, hand-drawn manga-style ink line art. Late-1990s Japanese street-racing anime style, dramatic high-contrast look, with a retro, slightly rough hand-inked feel: heavier black ink contour weight, faint pen-line wobble as if inked by hand frame by frame, a light halftone-dot shading pattern layered into the darkest shadow shapes, subtle scan-line grain across the frame, warm slightly desaturated retro color grading. Flat solid color fills with strong, clearly separated cel-shading — one hard-edged core shadow tone and a brighter secondary highlight tone per surface. A clean picture: the frame shows only the scene.

nodes.title: WORLD
widgets_values: The street on the outskirts of Shibuwaka, a small town in rural Japan, at clear midday: small shops with plain flat color signboards, a row of brightly colored drink vending machines, trimmed hedges, pastel apartment blocks with laundry-hung balconies, and utility poles with dense black cables sagging across a flat hazy pale sky. Daylight falls as hard-edged flat shadow shapes, with crisp flat highlights on painted metal and glass.

nodes.title: Presets
widgets_values:
## Presets – copy into THIS SHOT, change the CAPS

**1 · Character + VOICE LINE**
```
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is NAME in <Picture 1>, SHORT LOOK.

summary:
[reference generation] NAME says his line to the camera.

detailed_description:
{STYLE}

{WORLD}

[Shot 1] CAMERA. NAME (S1) speaks with ACTING, mouth exactly on the voice line: <d>[Japanese] THE LINE.</d> AFTER THE LINE.

overall_soundscape:
AMBIENCE.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A
```

**2 · AUDIO REFERENCE (new sentence)** – preset 1 plus this line in subject_definitions, and `in the voice from <Audio 1>` before the `<d>` line:
`<Audio 1> is NAME's voice: copy its timbre and accent; the words come from this prompt.`

**3 · Own acting (VIDEO REFERENCE, Follow acting)**
```
subject_definitions:
<Video 1> is my acting reference: WHAT HAPPENS IN THE CLIP.
<Subject 1> is NAME in <Picture 1>, SHORT LOOK.

summary:
[video editing + reference generation] The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>: camera, timing, every movement and the lip movement with its audio stay exactly as in <Video 1>; only the look changes: the person becomes <Subject 1>.

retention_analysis:
<Video 1>: fully_preserved - camera, framing, motion, timing, lips.
<Subject 1>: attribute_transfer - the look of <Picture 1> on the person of <Video 1>.
```
then `detailed_description` as in 1.

**4 · Blender layout (VIDEO REFERENCE)** – like 3, with `<Video 1> is a Blender layout render in grey placeholder materials …` and `fully_preserved - camera, layout, motion, timing; only surfaces change`. Say what every placeholder becomes. Frame-exact camera: MODE *Exact layout*.

**5 · Drawn-on start frame** – the drawing into START FRAME, switch it on, describe the action the arrows show.

**6 · Storyboard** – the board in REF IMAGE 1: `<Picture 1> is the storyboard: [Shot N] matches panel N in composition and camera.` One `[Shot N] At 00:0X.XXX, the shot cuts to …` per panel.
